title: Energy Gone? Perfectly Inelastic Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
Wet clay hits a wall and sticks. Two railway coaches couple up and roll away as one. And in the college lab, Aarav rolls a trolley into a still one with sticky pads: the pair rolls on at half the speed. Momentum is fine, but half the kinetic energy is gone. Where did it go? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 5, Work, Energy and Power) we learn the perfectly inelastic collision.

On a live motion notebook two trolleys crash and lock together, while the readout and a kinetic energy vs time graph show the total energy drop and never come back. A slow-mo replay freezes the crunch: equal and opposite pushes, a pad that stays squashed, and energy that turns into heat and sound. We derive the common velocity and the energy lost, Delta K = (1/2) m1m2/(m1 + m2) (u1 - u2)^2, step by step, show link by link why energy must be lost (K = p^2/2m), compare elastic and perfectly inelastic side by side, and work a full example. Then the exam trap (not all the kinetic energy is lost), an original JEE Main pattern question on a bullet stuck in a hanging block, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC (CISCE) and PUC (Karnataka) Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET preparation.
